comment: Cases the two implementations of the unfilled-template guard must
decide identically: unfilledKeys() in noyau/messages.ts, which arms
the banner the volunteer sees, and UnfilledKeys() in api/org.go, which
arms the server's refusal. Two implementations means the weaker one is
the one that counts, and a value let through reaches mayors verbatim.
Read by noyau/messages.test.ts and by api/config_test.go. Add a case
here and both languages must answer for it.
`value` is what the coordination typed into the campaign form;
`unfilled` is true when it must NOT be allowed to reach a mayor.

cases.value: équipe de campagne de Camille Durand

cases.why: the template with a double space — a copy-paste artefact
an invisible U+200B inside the template value
a non-breaking space inside the template value — Go's \s did not fold it
a narrow no-break space, what a French keyboard produces before punctuation
the template phone number typed with non-breaking spaces
U+0085 — JavaScript's \s left it alone while Go folded it
a trailing U+0085, which trim() folds and \s does not
the template with a decomposed é, as pasted from a PDF
curly placeholder — the natural thing to write, and it went out verbatim
